scope: Full exact-source review, all seven final expanded declaration types and all seven axiom reports for finite radial polynomial reduction, with targeted pinned-Mathlib evaluation/support/product semantics.
evidence_category: Lean kernel-compiled algebraic evaluation identity with explicit finite-support polynomial definitions. This is not an executable rational-polynomial implementation.

findings.check: Actual polynomial objects and variable convention
findings.reason: Input is a genuine MvPolynomial (Fin 4) R. The first three variables are mapped by Fin.castSucc, the fourth is Fin.last 3. Fin.snoc X r is exactly the evaluation map with these assignments. Output Even and Odd are genuine polynomials in only the three spatial variables.

Both outputs sum over exactly the actual finite support of P, retaining each actual coefficient. The common monomial core is product_i X_i^(d_i) times (sum_i X_i^2)^(d_r/2). Even retains only even radial exponents; Odd retains only odd radial exponents. No existential selection, unspecified decomposition or root selection appears.

For every natural k, k=2*(k/2)+k%2. The nonzero remainder is proved to be 1. Thus r^k=q^(k/2) times 1 for even k and r for odd k, assuming only r^2=q. The argument uses nonnegative integer powers, without division in the coefficient semiring.

The pinned eval_eq theorem expands P as the support sum of coefficient times the full coordinate product. prod_univ_castSucc isolates exactly the last radial factor. The proved monomial-core evaluation and power reduction establish each summand, and distributivity yields eval(P)=eval(Even(P))+r*eval(Odd(P)).

k=0 uses q^0=1 and the even branch, giving 1=1 even if r=q=0; k=1 gives r. Empty support gives both outputs zero for P=0. A constant monomial has radial exponent zero and contributes only to Even. Vanishing coordinates, zero coefficients, the trivial semiring and nilpotent elements require no exclusions. These checks are direct semantic specializations of the already universal compiled identities, not additional computational test certificates.

The theorem is universal over arbitrary CommSemiring R and P,X,r, conditional only on the advertised radial relation r^2=sum_i X_i^2. It requires no field, domain, characteristic-zero, positivity, norm, nonzero radius or analytic assumptions. The radial relation is the intended input variety condition, not the claimed polynomial reduction as a premise.

findings.check: Meaning of degree one in r
findings.reason: The output expression is syntactically A(X)+r*B(X) with A,B having no radial variable. This module does not yet assert total-degree, homogeneity, coefficient-norm or complexity bounds.

The definitions specify finite algebraic formulas, but the file explicitly uses noncomputable Mathlib MvPolynomial operations over arbitrary semirings. No executable Lean evaluator, rational-polynomial data structure, operation count or bit-cost theorem is supplied here.

limitations: This establishes equality of evaluations on the radial relation, not equality with P in the free four-variable polynomial ring.
Uniqueness of a normal form in a quotient ring and uniqueness from values on a real slice are not established here.
Homogeneous degree control, L1 coefficient bounds, invariant spinor polynomial decomposition and analytic convergence remain separate obligations.
The identification r=norm(y)^2 and X=ksMap(y) is supplied by a separate physical KS algebra theorem; the present module is a more general semiring identity.
No executable rational-polynomial implementation, certified finite energy solver, bit complexity or full Theorem T follows from this module alone.
The review reused existing compiler and strict-audit evidence and is not an isolated source-dependency rebuild.
